description:
What’s Flowing?

Conversations while everything changes.

What’s Flowing? is a walking podcast from Malmö, Sweden and part of the Everyday Flow ecosystem.

Each episode is recorded while walking. Sometimes it’s quiet. Most of the time it’s windy. Sometimes you can hear the city, the sea, a dog, footsteps, or life happening around us. That’s part of it.

Think of it as dropping into a phone call between two people who happen to be out for a walk,  talking, noticing, thinking out loud, following an idea and seeing where it goes.

Because walking does something to a conversation. When the body moves, ideas seem to move too. Thoughts connect differently. There’s less pressure to perform and more room for curiosity.


The host, Flavia Marfella, is an expat based in Malmö, Italian, who has spent years working with innovation, ideas and change. She’s also a podcaster, app developer, certified coach and positive psychology practitioner — curious by nature and always interested in what helps people, ideas and possibilities move forward.

This isn’t her first podcast — but this one feels different. Maybe it’s the timing: life changes, midlife shifts, priorities move, and the questions become less about having the right answers and more about staying curious about what’s unfolding.


We might talk about creativity, work, identity, technology, midlife, starting again, living abroad, relationships, wellbeing, or something completely unexpected. The point isn’t to tell you what to change next. It’s to stay curious about what’s already moving.


Everyday Flow is an evolving world of ideas, projects and experiences built around living with more curiosity, intention and flow. What’s Flowing? is its conversational side — a place to meet people, follow interesting threads and keep each other company while everything keeps changing.

No perfect studio. No formulas. No pressure to reinvent yourself.

Just put on your headphones and walk with us.

Let’s see what’s flowing.

title: A journey through feminist agroecology
author: CIDSE & AgroecologyNow-CAWR
description:
Why is agroecology not possible without feminism? What does feminism have to do with the food you eat? Agroecology is gaining steam as the way forward to sustainable, just and healthy food systems, however, there is still ample confusion about why the feminist perspective is important, how it aligns with agroecology and what it has to offer to food system transformation. It is often confused with gender equity, whereas feminist values include but go far beyond gender. 


In this podcast activists, researchers and practitioners who dedicate their lives to feminism and agroecology share how women (and others) are invisibly sustaining the food system, what it means to place ‘life’, rather than profit, in the centre of the food system, and what food systems would look like if they were based on feminist values. We explore how the oppression of women forms part of systemic oppression against anyone who falls out of the white, heterosexual, cis-male box, what decolonial and indigenous feminisms offer to the agroecology movement, and how to strengthen that movement from a feminist perspective. 


This podcast is a collaboration between The Centre for Agroecology, Water and Resilience (CAWR) and CIDSE.


This project has received funding from the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme under the Marie Sklodowska-Curie grant agreement No 844637.

title: Pink Hair, Ain't Scared
author: Marge
description:
Pink Hair Ain't Scared is a true scary storytelling podcast and I'm Marge, your spooky drag storyteller. I'm so glad you found me.


Every episode, I sit down with real stories. Submitted by real people or posted on the internet. These are things that actually happened. It's the kind of stuff that's too specific and too strange to explain away, like a shadow that keeps showing up... A sound that comes from the wrong room... A child who's made friends with something you can't see. I tell these stories honestly, unhurried, and with full respect for how terrifying they actually are.


What makes this show different? It's drag, honey! I bring the warmth, wit, and the occasional dramatic pause that turns an already-creepy story into something you feel in your chest. I'm not here to shock you. I'm here to sit with you in the dark for a little while.


No gimmicks. No dramatic sound design pretending to do the work (well, maybe some creepy music boxes). But really, it's just me, the stories, and you.


If you love paranormal podcasts, ghost stories, or anything that makes you double-check the hallway before bed, you're home! Follow Pink Hair Ain't Scared wherever you listen. Tell a friend. And maybe, just maybe, leave a light on.

The goal isn’t for me to act as an authority to tell you what the Bible says—it’s to encourage you to open the Scriptures, dig deeper, ask questions, and discover the richness of God’s Word for yourself!

Relationships, money, family, the weight of carrying everyone around him, and the parts of the story that don't make the highlight reel.

title: Wholehearted with Shawn Zajas
author: Shawn Zajas
description:
Somewhere along the way, a lot of good men lost heart.
Not their nerve — their heart. The part that used to hope, create, and believe it could still be good. It got buried under shame, under failure, under the quiet verdict that it's too late for them now.
Wholehearted is for those men.
This is a show about the who, not the what. I've spent years sitting across from people in the middle of their story — not the polished "after," the messy middle — and I've never gotten tired of the same thing: the beauty that comes out of brokenness when a person is finally seen and finally honest.
So that's what we do here. Real conversations with people who've walked through moral failure, loss, addiction, doubt, or the slow death of a dream — and found their way back to life. No advice. No fixing. No five-step formulas. Just presence, honesty, faith, and the stubborn belief that restoration is real and no one is past it.
If you're a man who's quietly given up on part of yourself — or you love someone who has — pull up a chair. You're not as far gone as the shame keeps telling you that you are.
It all starts at the root: becoming whole. From there comes authentic brilliance, and a life that creates something remarkable.
Hosted by Shawn Zajas.

title: A Cairos Moment the Podcast™
author: Jamia Anderson
description:
Imagine this:

You just quit your job. It's a role you once dreamed of attaining. And you spent more than a decade working towards it.

You had an unplanned baby, moved back to your parents' home, experienced financial and mental challenges and felt so lost.

It seemed as if everything was falling apart. But when God shows up in a mighty way one morning, you realize your season of wilderness is, in fact, not a storm.

It's God's appointed time to act.


A Cairos Moment is more than just a podcast. It's a passion project. It's purpose unfolding. It's what lives at the intersection of surrender, obedience, vulnerability, faith and favor.


Host Jamia Anderson, a journalist-turned-entrepreneur who knew she was called to more, invites listeners on a deeply personal journey of life after giving God her "Yes" and acting on her Kairos Moment.


Each of ACM's raw, heartfelt and inspiring episodes leave listeners with a thought-provoking question that might make you wonder if it's your time to act...

title: California Love
author: LAist Studios
description:
California Love is a blend of memoir, pop culture analysis and oral history. The newest season, K-Pop Dreaming, is about the rise and history of K-pop in the United States, as told from the point-of-view of the Korean diaspora in Los Angeles. Host Vivian Yoon takes listeners on a journey from K-pop’s origins in Korean trot music and American presence in post-war South Korea to the 1992 LA Uprising and the booming global popularity of K-pop in the present day, all juxtaposed against Yoon’s own coming-of-age as a second generation immigrant in Los Angeles, struggling to fit in and come to terms with her own identity.
In the first season Walter Thompson-Hernández was inspired by Tupac and Dr. Dre's "California Love"- a love letter and anthem for a generation. Walter invites listeners to join him in his family home, on horseback through the streets of Compton, and up into the sky to examine belonging.

description:
In a post-apocalyptic future, Marvel's Wastelanders: Star-Lord finds Peter Quill (Timothy Busfield) and Rocket (Chris Elliott) a little paunchier, a little slower, and a lot saltier than they were during the glory days of the Guardians of the Galaxy. They quickly discover the Earth isn't what it used to be either, when they crash land 30 years after all the world's super villains seized control.
The former Guardians are accompanied by a Rigellian Recorder, affectionately dubbed "Cora", who documents their mission to find the Black Vortex--an ancient relic reported to yield cosmic powers--before guillotine collars bestowed upon them by The Collector snap their necks. In the barren, desolate wasteland of the mid-west as controlled by Doctor Doom, they encounter the ageless telepath, Emma Frost, outlaw Ghost Riders, and the bloodthirsty Kraven the Hunter. Who will find the Black Vortex first and what will be the price of its power?
Written by Benjamin Percy (Wolverine: The Long Night, Wolverine: The Lost Trail), directed by Kimberly Senior (Disgraced), and sound designed with original scoring by Mark Henry Phillips (Homecoming, Passenger List). Learn more at marvel.com/wastelanders

Through personal stories and hard truths, this podcast is a reminder that what happened to you doesn’t have to define you. You were never too much, you were never alone, and your story doesn’t end where your pain began.

title: The Horatio Alger Jr. Library
author: Horatio Alger Jr.
description:
Step into the bustling streets, humble lodgings, counting rooms, and hopeful parlors of nineteenth-century America with The Horatio Alger Jr. Library.

Here you will hear, in full, the stories that made Horatio Alger Jr. one of the most widely read authors of his age: tales of poor boys, honest work, hard lessons, unexpected opportunity, and the determined climb toward respectability and independence.

These are stories of bootblacks, newsboys, clerks, strivers, and young men who discover that courage, thrift, perseverance, and good character may yet open a door where none seemed to exist.

If you have ever taken pleasure in an old-fashioned tale of adversity overcome, fortune earned, and hope rewarded, you will find much here to enjoy.

title: In The Dark
author: The New Yorker
description:
In the Dark, hosted by Madeleine Baran, is an award-winning investigative-journalism podcast that started in 2016. Its first season looked at the mysterious abduction of Jacob Wetterling in rural Minnesota and the lack of accountability that sheriffs face when they fail to solve cases. Season 2 examined the case of Curtis Flowers, who was tried six times for the same crime. In 2020, In the Dark released a special report on the coronavirus pandemic in the Mississippi Delta. In 2023, In the Dark joined The New Yorker and in 2024, it released “The Runaway Princesses,” a four-part series that asks why the women in Dubai’s royal family keep trying to run away. Season 3, released in 2024, asked why no one was punished for the killings of twenty-five civilians in Haditha, Iraq.
In the Dark won the Pulitzer Prize for audio for Season 3. The podcast is a three-time Peabody Award winner and, in 2019, became the first podcast to win a George Polk Award, one of the top honors in journalism. The program has also received an Alfred I. duPont-Columbia University Award and a Robert F. Kennedy Journalism Award.
New Yorker subscribers get early, ad-free access. In Apple Podcasts, tap the link at the top of the feed to subscribe or link an existing subscription. Or visit newyorker.com/dark to subscribe and listen in the New Yorker app.
If you have comments or story tips, please send them to inthedark@newyorker.com.

From suspicious corporate footprints to historical "missing years," we follow the breadcrumbs through real-world facts, documented scandals, and unsettling coincidences—then separate what's verified from what's speculation.

Have you ever looked at someone and thought...

"Wow... they really have it all together."

After more than three decades leading innovation and transformation in healthcare, and co-founding a company that helped millions of Canadians improve their health and wellbeing, Susanne retired to begin a different journey—one of understanding the story beneath her own life.

title: Honest Thoughts and Coffee
author: Dayna Horton
description:
Hi, I’m Dayna 🩵 Wife, mom of teens, full-time working mom, and navigating midlife one day at a time.

Honest Thoughts and Coffee is a podcast for women in midlife who are balancing motherhood, marriage, work, faith, health, and all the ordinary chaos that comes with this season of life.

Here we talk about midlife motherhood, parenting teenagers, marriage, Christian faith, realistic wellness, healthy aging, mindset, simple routines, and building a steady life—without extremes or perfection.

You’ll find honest conversations, practical wellness habits, everyday routines, faith-filled encouragement, and real-life perspective for becoming stronger, healthier, more grounded, and more intentional in midlife.

If you’re a working mom, wife, mom of teens, or woman navigating midlife, grab your coffee and pull up a chair.

title: We Are The Forest
author: Jacqui Croat
description: We are all the forest, whether you live in the city or the country, the plains or next to the sea. We are the forest because we can’t live without their life-giving oxygen, the rains that they draw toward them, the recycling of nutrients, the cleansing of waters as they pass through and the deep wisdom the trees carry for the entire world. On this podcast, we talk with wise people who have listened deeply to what the trees tell us about our inter-connectedness, our inter-dependence, the intelligence and magic of forests and ideas of how you can be more fully immersed in your forest.

description:
Monday Music Club is a podcast about the defining moments that have shaped the way we hear the world. Each week, host Will Anderson explores the stories behind iconic songs, legendary artists, and the creative forces that have transformed music and culture.

Will first rose to prominence as the frontman of the alternative pop band Parachute, earning platinum- and gold-certified singles while touring sold-out venues around the world. That firsthand experience, paired with an endless curiosity about music and its rich history, gives him a unique perspective on the people, innovations and cultural shifts that have soundtracked our lives.

Whether you’re obsessed with music history, fascinated by the craft of songwriting, or simply looking to hear your favorite songs in a new way, Monday Music Club is where the conversation begins.

The name represents being “unlocked” through real conversations, new perspectives, and the truth behind the journey.

title: The Forbidden Truth

description:
Uncovering the stories they don’t want you to hear.
Step beyond the headlines and into the shadows. The Forbidden Truth is a bold, unapologetic podcast that dives deep into the conspiracy theories, political cover-ups, and suppressed stories the mainstream refuses to touch. Hosted with fearless curiosity and a commitment to truth, each episode exposes the hidden forces shaping our world.
If you're tired of censorship, propaganda, and one-sided narratives, this is where you will find the hard questions and uncomfortable truths. 
Sometimes, the truth isn’t just hidden — it’s forbidden.

title: Science Channel

description:
Leadership Happy Hour is where leaders pour a drink, skip the theory, and talk about what actually makes them better.
Each week, Certified Executive Coach Alesia Briggs sits down with sharp operators, coaches, and executives for a real conversation you can use right away. The industry and title change every week. What stays the same: they've all made the decision to show up.
Pull up a seat. New episodes drop every week. Find Alesia at coachbriggs.com.

title: Soft Power Esra
author: Esra
description:
What if growth didn't come from pressure, but from choosing ourselves?
Welcome to Soft Power — a place for the conversations we usually only have with ourselves.
I'm Esra, and every week I invite you into my inner world. Through stories of love, heartbreak, travel, healing, friendship, anxiety, and the quiet moments in between, I try to put feelings into words that many of us struggle to explain.
This isn't a podcast about having all the answers.
It's about asking better questions.
Because sometimes we don't need advice.
Sometimes we just need someone to say,
"I've felt that too."

title: H.U.E. The Two Choices Podcast
author: Lorenzo E Bland Jr
description: Every person faces a definitive ultimatum. In H.U.E. The Two Choice Podcast, we delve into the dual paths of human existence and the ultimate choice you must make. You can either become Hell's Ultimate Enemy by embracing the continuous, evolving journey of life, or Heaven's Ultimate Enemy by accepting the stark, absolute finality of death. There is no middle ground. Which enemy will you choose to be? Tune in as we explore the deep philosophical, spiritual, and existential realities of the two choices that define us all.

author: Zahid Awan
description:
Conquer the Mind, Conquer the World is a podcast about mastering the mind — where ancient wisdom and modern neuroscience meet. Host Zahid Awan brings a rare mix of backgrounds to the conversation: years as a defense and foreign affairs journalist, two decades as a licensed realtor, training as a certified yoga and breathwork teacher, and now a Master of Social Work candidate preparing to move into clinical mental health work.
Drawing from his book Echoes of Light: Decoding the Nervous System for Inner Mastery, each episode breaks down how the nervous system shapes stress, resilience, and healing — pairing hard science with practices that go back thousands of years. Expect honest, practical conversations and simple tools you can use the same day you listen.
Whether you're curious about neuroscience, exploring mindfulness, or just trying to handle life's stress a little better, this show is your guide to understanding — and mastering — the mind.

title: Heard Not Hushed
author: Piers Day
description: Heard Not Hushed is for anyone who wants to understand what's really going on beneath the silence. Drawing on 27 years working with young people on mental health and emotional wellbeing, Piers Day shares the patterns he's seen and sits down with people who've lived through the moments that get hushed instead of heard — the crises, the turning points, the things families don't know how to say out loud. Every episode leaves you with something to think about, and something you can actually do.

title: Letitia Kapuscinska's podcast
author: Letitia Kapuscinska
description:
LETITIA ANTOINETTE — Conversations Beyond the Ordinary

Hosted by Hon. Prof. Amb. Dr. Duchess Letitia Antoinette Kapuscinska, internationally known as Madame Kapuscinska, the Letitia Antoinette Podcast is a global platform for thought-provoking conversations, lived experience, creativity, leadership, wellbeing, entrepreneurship and positive social impact.

What began as a space for Letitia to explore her thoughts and experiences has evolved into a platform bringing together artists, entrepreneurs, academics, innovators, community leaders, change-makers and extraordinary people from around the world.

A singer-songwriter, author, broadcaster, complementary therapist, entrepreneur, business consultant, educator and thought leader, Letitia draws upon a multidisciplinary career spanning music, media, holistic wellbeing, education, business, humanitarian initiatives and the creative industries.

Expect honest conversations about success and adversity, identity, purpose, mental wellbeing, relationships, spirituality, business, music, creativity, leadership, education and the realities behind people’s achievements.

Some episodes are inspiring. Some are challenging. Some are deeply personal. All are driven by curiosity and the belief that meaningful conversation can educate, connect and transform.

This show only cares about the receipt: real vulnerabilities found in real software, reported responsibly, and fixed and credited by real vendors. Short episodes, plain language, public proof. Built by the founder of an autonomous AI engine that hunts vulnerabilities around the clock.

title: דרך החן: גירושין, הורות ויחסים
author: Khen Tsubery
description:
״דרך החן״ הוא פודקאסט על גירושין, הורות ויחסים, ועל הדרך שבה אנחנו יכולים להגיע לחיים טובים יציבים ומאושרים, על אף ובזכות המהמורות שבדרך.
נדבר כאן על גירושין מכל הזוויות: משנות ההתלבטות, דרך ניהול תהליך הפרידה, ועד החיים שאחריו כמשפחה שחיה בשני בתים. נעסוק בשמירה על הילדים, בבניית תקשורת מיטיבה בין ההורים ובהתאמת ההורות למציאות המשתנה.
אבל נצא גם הרבה מעבר לגירושין. נדבר על הורות, מערכות יחסים, טראומה וריפוי, זהות, בחירות ותהליכי צמיחה.
אני חן צוברי, עובדת סוציאלית קלינית, מדריכת הורים ומגשרת לגירושין. בכל פרק אביא ידע מקצועי, זוויות מחשבה חדשות ושיחות כנות על הרגעים המורכבים שכולנו פוגשים בדרך.

title: The Evolving Signal™
author: Jazzmyn Lauff
description:
The Evolving Signal™ is a living record of what becomes possible when recognition is trusted enough to participate—before we know where it will lead.
Each episode begins with an encounter: another person, perspective, discipline, worldview, species, generation, culture, or expression of consciousness. Not to arrive at a shared answer, but to notice what becomes recognizable through participation that could not have emerged otherwise.
Recognition is welcomed more than certainty. Curiosity remains in relationship with discernment. And every vantage point reveals something different.
These are encounters with the evolving signal—within us, between us, and throughout the living field we share.

title: The Beaver Tools

A collection of focused utilities for files, images, archives, and everyday workflow tasks.
No subscriptions, no clutter — just tools that do their job well.

title: Beyond the Dust
author: Michael Jason
description: What happens after the world shifts beneath your feet? Beyond the Dust explores the aftermath of life's biggest disruptions—the sudden loss, the unexpected pivot, and the moments that shatter our plans into pieces. Moving past superficial self-help and short-lived motivation, this show delves into the grit required to rebuild from the ground up. Through deep, unfiltered conversations and practical insights, Beyond the Dust examines how to uncover lasting purpose, restore identity, and forge a resilient path forward when the dust finally settles.

title: Extraordinary History
author: The Extraordinary Network LLC
description:
History did not happen in neat chapters. It unfolded day by day, through people who rarely understood how far the consequences of their actions would reach.

Each Sunday, the Extraordinary History Podcast journeys through the seven dates ahead, uncovering the remarkable events, people, discoveries, and decisions connected to that week. Traveling across centuries and continents, every episode transforms history from a collection of facts into immersive stories of human ambition, courage, ingenuity, conflict, and consequence.

Extraordinary History is thoughtful, intellectually satisfying storytelling for curious adults who believe the past remains one of humanity’s greatest stories.

title: The White Glove Podcast
author: White Glove
description:
Welcome to your destination of choice for rich, in-depth cricket stories. 
Tired of drama-filled hot takes? Looking for analytical deep dives and the human side of cricket? You’re in the right place. 
Junk journalism is not our thing. Instead, we serve you slow-cooked content that is healthy for the mind and therapeutic for your soul. 
We’re not the noise of cricket, we want to be the voice of cricket. 
If you are someone who values the written word, please visit our website thewhiteglove.in and check out the awesome literary reportage we’re doing.

description:
Life, Love and Lesson’s in your 20’s. Life in your 20s is messy, magical, and full of lessons and I’m here to talk about it all. From navigating relationships, learning from mistakes, and growing up, to tackling life’s biggest questions… no topic is off-limits. Real talk. Real views. Real life.
Tune in, laugh, reflect, and grow with me because life is too short for boring conversations. 💜✨

I sit down with Habib, my AI conversation partner, to talk about the things people actually think about but do not always say out loud.Family, marriage, divorce, parenting, faith, culture, relationships, addiction, loneliness, business, life experiences and everything in between.

Sometimes the conversation is serious. Sometimes it is personal. Sometimes I disagree with Habib completely. That is part of it.This is not a podcast about artificial intelligence. It is a podcast about human life, explored through a conversation between a human and AI.

description: Blockbuster Recovery is a podcast about what the movies can teach us about surviving hard things, rebuilding our lives, and becoming who we were meant to be. Through iconic films, honest conversations, special guests, and lived experience, Nate McGill and Sam Johnson explore addiction, trauma, faith, resilience, redemption, and personal transformation. It is a show for anyone who believes recovery is not simply about what we leave behind. It is about the life we choose to build next.

title: Brianna & Ryan

Brianna & Ryan is a podcast where real conversations meet unexpected stories, mysteries, relationships, and the moments that keep us thinking long after the episode ends. Join Brianna and Ryan as they explore fascinating topics, share personal perspectives, and uncover stories that are sometimes funny, sometimes unsettling, and always worth hearing.

From famous fast-food restaurants to hidden menu favorites, Explore with Daniel brings you simple, useful, and interesting food guides to help you decide what to order. Listen, explore, and discover your next favorite meal with Daniel! 🎙️🍽️

A podcast about the hidden powers of your menstrual cycle, your hormones, and the parts of womanhood nobody really explains , hosted like a conversation with the big sister you never had. Each week is honest, unfiltered, and real: no perfection, no scripts, just the truth about what it means to actually know your body and trust yourself again…. yes my love, that is possible! 
A space to finally feel seen, leaving every episode reminded that you are the expert of your own body.

description:
BOTO Daily | AI Daily Intelligence System
BOTO Daily is an AI-powered Global Decision Intelligence platform produced and supervised by the Zhiweizi Team.
Our goal is not to report every piece of news. Every day, we filter a vast amount of global information and identify the developments that truly matter to the economy, financial markets, global liquidity, and digital assets — helping you understand what matters and make better decisions in just five minutes.
【WHAT BOTO DAILY MONITORS EVERY DAY】
1. Global Risk
U.S.–Iran relations, U.S.–Israel military activity, Middle East tensions, the Strait of Hormuz, Red Sea shipping, global energy supply, and other major geopolitical risks that may affect global financial markets.
2. U.S. Economy & Global Liquidity
CPI, PPI, PCE, Non-Farm Payrolls, unemployment, GDP, PMI/ISM, retail sales, FOMC decisions, Federal Reserve policy, and important speeches by Fed officials.
We also monitor the Japanese yen, U.S. Treasury markets, the U.S. dollar, and other important liquidity signals that could trigger major shifts in global capital flows.
3. Bitcoin Core Data
Bitcoin price and market direction;
USDT, USDC, and total stablecoin supply;
U.S. spot Bitcoin ETF flows;
BTC exchange reserves;
Realized Price and the market’s average cost basis;
Short-Term Holder Cost Basis;
Long-Term Holder Cost Basis and accumulation or distribution;
Bitcoin’s correlation with U.S. equities;
CryptoQuant 30-day Spot Demand, Futures and Perpetual Demand, and Total Demand.
Together, these indicators help us understand Bitcoin’s real liquidity, supply-demand structure, and market cost basis.
4. Ethereum
We monitor ETF flows, major network upgrades, regulatory developments, and significant ecosystem changes.
5. AI · Web3 · BOTO Industry Intelligence
We focus on meaningful developments in artificial intelligence, Hyperliquid, Web3, data products, automation, and decision intelligence — including product innovation, user growth, funding, partnerships, and technological developments worth watching.
6. Major Global Developments
Every day, we select one or two major developments that could affect the global economy, financial markets, energy, supply chains, technology, AI, or global capital flows.
These developments are not limited to our regular monitoring categories. If an event is important enough, BOTO Daily will follow it.
【OUR DAILY PRINCIPLE】
We monitor our core indicators every day, but we do not repeatedly discuss data that has not meaningfully changed.
If there is no significant change, we simply state that it remains unchanged.
Every episode focuses on four questions:
What changed today?
Why does it matter?
What could it affect?
What should we watch next?
Important data must come from official or industry-recognized sources. Unverified information will never be presented as confirmed fact.
Filter Information. Identify Change.
Less Noise. More Insight. Better Decisions.
All in BOTO DAILY.

title: 100 Days Your Way | What It Actually Felt Like
author: Try Dry
description:
What It Actually Felt Like
Real stories from people changing their relationship with alcohol

Changing your relationship with alcohol is rarely straightforward. It is not linear, it is not always dramatic, and it does not look the same for everyone. What It Actually Felt Like is a series of honest, personal stories from people who have been through it, reflecting on the moments, realisations and turning points that shaped their journey.

Each episode focuses on a specific stage of the process: the early days when alcohol seems to be everywhere, the social situations that felt loaded, the difficult moments that almost derailed everything, and the quiet shifts that made things feel possible again. These are not polished success stories. They are honest accounts of what it actually felt like from the inside.

The series is part of 100 Days Your Way, a behaviour change programme from Alcohol Change UK designed to help people better understand and gradually take control of their relationship with alcohol. 100 Days Your Way is not a challenge or an abstinence programme. It is a 100-day guided experiment built around how habits actually work and how people genuinely change over time.


Whether you are at the start of your own journey or somewhere in the middle, you will find something in these episodes that feels familiar. And sometimes, hearing someone else describe exactly what you are going through is the most useful thing of all.

 Find out more about 100 Days Your Way at alcoholchange.org.uk

description:
I grew up knowing exactly how the world would end. What I didn’t know was that the theology I’d been handed and the God of the actual Gospels were not telling the same story.


From the Wilderness is a theology podcast for people who took their faith seriously and got burned by the institutions that were supposed to hold it. Each episode traces the real cost of church hurt, ministry burnout, and the eschatology that taught a generation to wait for rescue instead of showing up for each other. This is not a deconstruction podcast that ends in cynicism. It’s a reconstruction, built from real formation, real seminary training, and real loss, toward a faith sturdy enough to survive contact with an actual human life.


If you grew up on the Left Behind series, The Late Great Planet Earth, classical dispensationalism, and a sinner’s prayer that never quite answered your hardest questions, you are the reason this show exists. description: Inhumanities is a daily experimental podcast about what happens to the humanities when thought is routed through artificial intelligence.Part research diary, part theory show, part live laboratory, it follows encounters between literature, philosophy, media theory, cybernetics, AI systems, occult mathematics, internet subcultures, and experimental art practice. Episodes begin with a text, image, argument, archive, or technical procedure and push it through contemporary machine-assisted research until something unfamiliar emerges.The emphasis is not “AI explaining the humanities.” It is the stranger feedback loop: humans reading machines, machines reading culture, and both changing the conditions under which interpretation happens.Expect CCRU and the numogram beside Hamlet and theology; agentic workflows beside avant-garde publishing; archival research beside memes, group chats, image systems, and computational experiments.Inhumanities documents the humanities after they have entered the machine.
